claim: During the 2007-09 financial crisis, US industrial companies cut back repurchases sharply but continued to pay dividends, with dividend payout ratios largely unaffected by the crisis; dividends and repurchases both rebounded strongly by 2010.
stance_target: the query's claim that buybacks are pro-cyclical and shrink when cash flow weakens, while dividends are sticky
quoted_support: During the crisis industrials cut back repurchases sharply but continued to pay dividends, with payout ratios largely unaffected by the crisis. Dividends and repurchases rebound strongly in 2010.

claim: In 2007, at the peak of the pre-crisis payout boom, US industrial firms as a group paid out 90% of aggregate earnings via combined dividends and repurchases.
stance_target: sustainability of aggregate payout levels prior to a downturn
quoted_support: This trend fueled the explosive growth of payouts through 2007, when industrials paid out 90% of aggregate earnings.

claim: Unlike industrials, US financial firms cut back dividends aggressively as the 2007-09 crisis took hold, despite an initial reluctance to cut dividends even among TARP-recipient banks -- financials' dividend behavior during the crisis was less resilient than industrials'.
stance_target: whether dividend stickiness through downturns generalizes across sectors (it does not for financials)
scope_conditions: US financial firms including TARP recipients, 2007-2009
quoted_support: Financials cut back dividends aggressively as the crisis takes hold, although they too evidence a reluctance to cut dividends at the beginning of the crisis, including for the TARP banks.

claim: The authors find no evidence that the 2003 Tax Relief Act (which eliminated the tax disadvantage of dividends relative to capital gains) shifted the mix of payouts toward dividends; if anything the mix shifted further toward repurchases, and payout ratios did not rise -- inconsistent with taxes having a first-order effect on payout policy.
stance_target: tax-based explanations for dividend versus repurchase choice
quoted_support: In the years after the Tax Relief Act there is no evidence of a shift in the mix of dividends and repurchases towards dividends—if anything, the reverse is true. Nor is there evidence of an increase in dividend payout ratios.
